profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged telecom=data_center, is named "Factory Software | AVEVA Select Italia." AVEVA is a real, publicly traded industrial software company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that provides engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software used across manufacturing, energy, and process industries worldwide. "AVEVA Select" is the branding AVEVA uses for its network of regional reseller and systems-integrator partners, and this record most plausibly identifies an Italian partner office selling and supporting AVEVA's software products under that program, likely operating under the name "Factory Software" as the local reseller entity. A software reseller and integrator's office maintains its own business IT systems but is not a data-center operator; the telecom=data_center tag here is best read as a mistag of the office's own server or IT closet.

reading.body:
This record is a mistagged software office, not a data center. The OpenStreetMap point carries a telecom=data_center tag, but its name identifies an Italian reseller of AVEVA industrial software, and the research note concludes it is a partner office rather than a compute facility.

The distinction matters because data-center counts drawn from open mapping data are only as good as their tags. A single reseller office with a server closet can enter a dataset as a facility, and nothing in this record reports power draw, floor area, or installed capacity. The megawatt figure is zero, which is consistent with an office and tells you nothing about actual AI load.

What this does not cover is the scale of the error. One mistag is not evidence that open data on data centers is unreliable in general, and no count of similar cases is given here. The record also cannot say whether the underlying site hosts any meaningful compute at all, only that the tag is best read as a mistake.
